title: Spring has come, saqi
takeaway: Nothing in this world lasts, so love fully now, and don't fear the end.
scene: The rain clouds have finally come after a long dry spell, and spring is here. The poet turns to the saqi, the one pouring at the gathering, and starts talking about life, death and love.

original: بڑے چراں پچھوں بدلی چڑھی اج اے، ویکھ ساقیا آئی بہار ہے وے
ویلا لنگھیا فیر نئیں ہتھ آونا، سماں کدے نہ کسے دا یار ہے وے
transliteration: Bare chiraan pichhon badli charhi ajj ae, vekh saaqiya aayi bahaar hai ve
Vela langhiya pher nahin hatth aauna, samaan kade na kise da yaar hai ve
translation: After so long, the clouds have gathered today; look, saqi, spring has come.
Once time has passed it won't come back; time is never anyone's friend.
couplets.story: After a long wait, the clouds are back and spring has arrived. The poet tells the saqi to look. This is the moment. Once it's gone, you can't get it back. Time doesn't wait for anybody.

original: ایہہ سارا جہان ہے دکھ بھریا کسے تائیں نہ صبر قرار ہے وے
اساں منیا موت نے آونا ایں، کِنے چرتوں پر انتظار ہے وے
transliteration: Eh saara jahaan hai dukh bhariya, kise taaeen na sabr qaraar hai ve
Asaan manniya maut ne aauna ain, kinne chiraan ton par intezaar hai ve
translation: This whole world is full of sorrow; no one has patience or peace.
We accept that death must come, but oh, how long we've been waiting.
couplets.story: Everyone in this world is hurting in some way, and nobody is truly at peace. The poet knows death will come one day. He even seems tired of waiting for it.

original: ایس جگ وچ ساڈا نہ کوئی سجن، ساڈا کوئی نہ یار غم خوار ہے وے
اینان اتھروہڑاں نوں کون روکے، قول تیرا تے ریت دیوار ہے وے
transliteration: Is jag vich saada na koi sajan, saada koi na yaar gham-khaar hai ve
Inaan athru-harraan nu kaun rokay, qaul tera te ret deevaar hai ve
translation: In this world I have no friend, no companion to share my grief.
Who can hold back this flood of tears? Your promise is a wall of sand.
couplets.story: He feels he has no real friend here, no one who shares his pain. His tears pour like a flood. The beloved's promise was supposed to hold them back, but it was only a wall made of sand.

original: پلا جھاڑ کے یار نہ توں جائیں، اوکھا ہجر وچ تیرا بیمار ہے وے
اوہ ہولکیاں توڑ نبھاوندے نیں، جنہاں سجناں عشق دی سار ہے وے
transliteration: Palla jhaar ke yaar na toon jaaeen, aukha hijr vich tera beemaar hai ve
Oh holkiyaan tor nibhaunde nain, jinhaan sajnaan ishq di saar hai ve
translation: Friend, don't shake off your hem and walk away; the one sick with love for you is suffering.
Those who truly understand love keep faith right to the end.
couplets.story: He begs the beloved not to brush him off and leave. He is sick from missing them. People who really understand love, he says, stay loyal all the way.

original: دل دے دتا جان وار دتی، تُساں تائیں نہ اجے اعتبار ہے وے
ہیراں چڑھن ڈولی آخر کھیڑیاں دی، کچا تساں دا قول اقرار ہے وے
transliteration: Dil de ditta jaan vaar ditti, tusaan taaeen na ajje aitbaar hai ve
Heeraan charhan doli aakhir Kheriyaan di, kachcha tusaan da qaul iqraar hai ve
translation: I gave my heart and offered my life, and still you don't trust me.
In the end Heers climb into the Kheras' bridal palanquin; your vows are weak.
couplets.story: He has given everything, his heart and even his life, and the beloved still doesn't believe him. He remembers Heer, who promised herself to Ranjha but was married off to the Kheras in the end. Promises like that break easily.

original: ایسا درد فراق نے چھنڈیا اے، طاقت پیراں تے ہُن کھلون دی نئیں
تیری جھات حیاتی نوں بدل دیوے، ویکھن ہون لاگے تڑفے پیار ہے وے
transliteration: Aisa dard firaaq ne chhandiya ae, taaqat pairaan te hun khalon di nahin
Teri jhaat hayaati nu badal deve, vekhan hon laage tarfe pyaar hai ve
translation: The pain of separation has shaken me so badly my legs can't hold me up.
One glance from you would change my life; love is aching just to see you.
couplets.story: Missing the beloved has worn him out so much he can barely stand. But just one look from them would change everything. His whole heart is aching for that one look.

original: ایہہ لوک جنہوں موت آکھدے نیں، اک کھیڈ ہے تیرے دیوانیاں دی
سانوں موت توں پیا ڈراؤناں ایں، سانوں موت دے نال پیار ہے وے
transliteration: Eh lok jinhu maut aakhde nain, ik khed hai tere deewaaniyaan di
Saanu maut ton piya daraaunaa ain, saanu maut de naal pyaar hai ve
translation: What people call death is just a game to those who are mad for you.
You're trying to scare me with death? I love death.
couplets.story: Most people are terrified of dying. Not him. For people who love the way he does, death is nothing to fear. Someone tries to scare him with it, and he answers that he actually loves death.

original: رنگ روپ جوانی دا مان کاہدا، اینان سدا نہ کسے دے نال رہنا
نہ بلبلاں نے سدا چہکنا ایں، نہ سدا ای باغ بہار ہے وے
transliteration: Rang roop jawaani da maan kaahda, inaan sada na kise de naal rehna
Na bulbulaan ne sada chehakna ain, na sada ee baagh bahaar hai ve
translation: Why be proud of beauty, looks and youth? They won't stay with anyone forever.
The nightingales won't always sing, and the garden won't always be in bloom.
couplets.story: Good looks and being young feel like they'll last forever, but they don't, for anyone. The birds won't always be singing, and spring won't last. So there's no point being vain about any of it.

original: ایویں بدل نہ زاہد خیال میرا، مینوں رہن دے مست خیال اندر
عاشق توں تے حور قصور دا ایں، مینوں بندیاں نال پیار ہے وے
transliteration: Aiven badal na zaahid khayaal mera, mainu rehn de mast khayaal andar
Aashiq toon te hoor qasoor da ain, mainu bandiyaan naal pyaar hai ve
translation: Holy man, don't bother trying to change my mind; let me stay lost in my thoughts.
You're in love with heaven's maidens and palaces; I love human beings.
couplets.story: A strict religious man keeps lecturing him. The poet tells him to give up. The holy man is really chasing a reward, the beautiful companions and palaces of paradise. The poet says his love is for people, here and now.

original: زخماں باجھ نہ ٹیس دا مزا آوے، درداں باجھ نہ اتھرو وگدے نیں
احمدؔ ہجر دا گیت ہے چھیڑ بہندا، جدوں کھڑکدی عشق دی تار ہے وے
transliteration: Zakhmaan baajh na tees da maza aave, dardaan baajh na athru vagde nain
Ahmad hijr da geet hai chhed behnda, jadon kharakdi ishq di taar hai ve
translation: Without wounds you can't know the sweetness of the ache; without pain tears don't flow.
Ahmad starts singing the song of separation whenever love's string is plucked.
couplets.story: He ends by saying pain has its own strange sweetness. You can't feel it unless you've been hurt. Whenever love tugs at his heart like a string on an instrument, he can't help it. He starts singing about missing someone.

deeper:
This is one of the most openly Sufi poems in the book. The saqi pouring at the gathering is a classic picture of God, or of a spiritual guide, pouring out love. Saying 'I love death' sounds shocking, but for Sufis death is the moment the soul finally meets the Beloved, so they call it a wedding, not an ending.

The couplet about the holy man is the key. Sufis said that worshipping God only for the rewards of paradise is like working for wages. Real love wants God Himself, and shows itself in loving His people. That's why the poet says, 'I love human beings.'

There is also a line about what the poet values most. He tells the holy man: you love heaven's maidens, but 'I love human beings'. For him, love for God has to show up as love for people here and now.
why: It packs a lot of big ideas into simple pictures: time doesn't wait, youth doesn't last, love matters more than rewards, and pain can make you more alive.
prompt: Do you do good things for a reward, or because you care? How can you tell the difference?
notes: Couplet 4, line 2: 'holkiyaan tor' is read as 'right to the end'.
Couplet 6, line 2 is slightly unclear in the print; the general sense is kept.
